AMZN_2010_p33__paragraph_1.ocr:
We have organized our operations into two principal segments: North America and International. We
present our segment information along the same lines that our chief executive reviews our operating results in
assessing performance and allocating resources.

AMZN_2010_p33__caption_1.ocr: Net sales information is as follows:

AMZN_2010_p33__paragraph_2.ocr:
Sales increased 40%, 28%, and 29% in 2010, 2009, and 2008. Changes in currency exchange rates
positively (negatively) affected net sales by $(86) million, $(182) million, and $127 million for 2010, 2009, and
2008. For a discussion of the effect on sales growth of exchange rates, see “Effect of Exchange Rates” below.

AMZN_2010_p33__paragraph_3.ocr:
The North America sales growth rate was 46%, 25%, and 26% in 2010, 2009, and 2008. The sales growth in
each year primarily reflects increased unit sales, a larger base of sales in faster growing categories such as
electronics and other general merchandise, and, in 2010, our adoption of the new accounting standard update
(“ASU”) 2009-13 (see Item 8 of Part II, “Financial Statements and Supplementary Data—Note 1—Description
of Business and Accounting Policies”). Increased unit sales were driven largely by our continued efforts to
reduce prices for our customers, including from our free shipping offers and Amazon Prime, by increased
in-stock inventory availability and increased selection of product offerings, and by the impact of Zappos, which
we acquired in the fourth quarter of 2009.
